notes: Authored fictional English inputs. Expectations test conservative topic shortlisting, not funding eligibility. Live AI extraction is a separate evaluation and may omit uncertain values.

cases.title: Forest fire early warning
cases.description: We are a small software company (SME) registered in Portugal. We built solar-powered forest cameras with AI software that detects smoke and warns local fire teams. Our prototype was tested in three forests and detected controlled fires within 90 seconds. Two municipalities expressed interest in paid pilots, but no agreements are signed yet. We will commercialise the technology by improving the detection model, running larger field trials and preparing to manufacture more cameras for southern Europe. We request EUR 120,000 funding. Total project cost is EUR 180,000; we plan to pay EUR 60,000 from company savings. We have not yet measured false alarms or compared our system with existing monitoring.
cases.explanation: Fictional project: cameras warn fire teams when AI detects smoke. Early forest tests make the idea worth investigating. Detection speed alone does not prove reliability or superiority: false alarms and comparison tests are missing. Municipal interest is not a signed paid pilot. The deeper review should explain those gaps and help prepare a test, customer and spending plan.

cases.title: Wind turbine fault detector
cases.description: We are a small software company (SME) registered in Ireland. We built software that spots early faults in wind turbines from sensor readings, and tested a prototype at one wind farm. We will commercialise it by running field trials at more farms and getting it ready to sell across Europe. The total project cost is EUR 180,000 for two engineers, sensors and field trials, and independent security testing. We request EUR 120,000 funding and will pay the remaining EUR 60,000 ourselves.
cases.explanation: This is a fictional example, not an approved project. One possible EUR 180,000 budget is EUR 100,000 for two engineers, EUR 50,000 for sensors and field trials, and EUR 30,000 for independent testing. The company would pay EUR 60,000 itself and request EUR 120,000. EIC Accelerator is only a topic lead: reviewers would still need proof of the technology, market, team and budget. The older EIC Transition call has extra research-history rules.

cases.title: Less waste in a metal factory
cases.description: We are a small manufacturing company (SME) registered in Germany. We make metal parts for electric buses. We will develop a prototype that uses less metal to make each part. We will install energy-saving equipment on the test line. The total project cost is EUR 800,000. It covers prototype machinery, engineers and factory testing. We request EUR 500,000 funding. We will pay EUR 300,000 ourselves.
cases.explanation: The company wants to test a less wasteful production line. The EUR 800,000 cost covers equipment, engineering and trials, with EUR 300,000 paid by the company. Research programmes may be worth checking, but international partners and the exact challenge topics remain unverified.

cases.title: Plastic recycling — closed calls
cases.description: We are a small recycling company (SME) registered in the Netherlands. We will recycle plastic offcuts from factories into new packaging material. We will install water-saving equipment to wash the plastic. The total project cost is EUR 700,000. It covers sorting and washing machines, site changes and testing. We request EUR 400,000 funding. We will pay EUR 300,000 ourselves.
cases.explanation: The company would buy sorting and washing equipment and test a way to reuse factory plastic. The matching LIFE rounds in this demo are closed, so this is a research lead for future calls, not an application opportunity today.

cases.title: Farm software in Canada — open in demo
cases.explanation: The company would pay for research and a local partner to find out whether Canadian farms would buy its existing product. Innowwide's recorded call is open in this fixed-date demo, but company age, partner and cost rules still need checking.
cases.description: We are a small software company (SME) registered in Ireland. We sell software that helps farms spot crop disease from satellite images. We will conduct a market feasibility study in Canada: interview farmers, check local rules and work with a Canadian partner to see whether farms would buy it. The total project cost is EUR 86,000 for local research, travel and the partner's work. We request EUR 60,000 funding and will pay EUR 26,000 ourselves.
